lesson.title: React useEffect() hook introduction
lesson.goal: learn the React useEffect hook: run side effects on mount and on state changes, and clean them up

steps.title: Set up counter component
steps.instructions: Scaffold a React app (npm create vite@latest my-app -- --template react), then create src/MyComponent.jsx importing useState and useEffect, with a count state, a `Count: {count}` paragraph and an Add button calling addCount (setCount(c => c + 1)). Render it from App.jsx and run npm run dev.

targets.caption: The count state variable starting at zero
Handler that adds one using the previous state
The rendered count paragraph

explanations.topic: Importing useState and useEffect from React
Creating a state variable and its setter with initial value 0
Using an updater function with the previous state to increment

hints: Start by importing both hooks from 'react' in one import statement.
Declare state with array destructuring: const [count, setCount] = useState(0).

Render a

showing Count: {count} and a
Inside addCount call setCount(c => c + 1) so it uses the previous state.
common_mistakes: Writing onClick={addCount()}, which calls the function during render and causes an infinite re-render loop.
Forgetting to import useEffect (or useState) from 'react'.
Returning two sibling elements without wrapping them in a fragment <> </> or a div.
Forgetting to render the component in App.jsx, so nothing appears in the browser.

steps.title: Update title on every render
steps.instructions: In MyComponent, call useEffect with an arrow function and no dependency array that sets document.title = `Count: ${count}`. Click Add and confirm the tab title updates each render.

targets.caption: Call useEffect with no dependency array
Set the title to a template string containing count

explanations.topic: useEffect runs side code every time the component re-renders
useEffect takes two arguments: a function and an array of dependencies
Omitting the dependency array runs the effect on every render
The effect also runs initially when the component mounts

hints: Import useEffect from 'react' alongside useState, then call it inside your component near the top.
Pass useEffect a single arrow function and leave out the second argument so it runs after every render.
Inside the arrow function, assign a template string to document.title, inserting your count state variable with ${count}.
Save, refresh the browser, and click Add. The browser tab's title should change to show the new count each time.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to import useEffect from 'react', which gives 'useEffect is not defined'.
Passing an empty array [] as the second argument at this point, which makes the title update only on mount.
Using regular quotes instead of backticks, so ${count} shows up literally in the title.
Calling useEffect outside the component or inside a condition or handler instead of at the top level of the component.
Writing document.title(...) as a function call instead of assigning to it with =

steps.title: Run effect only on mount
steps.instructions: Add useEffect with an empty dependency array [] that sets document.title (e.g. 'My Counter Program'). Confirm the title is set once and does not change on clicks.

targets.caption: Empty dependency array: the effect runs only on mount
One-time side effect that sets the page title

explanations.topic: Empty dependency array means the effect runs only on mount
Title updates once and never after clicks
One-and-done effects such as a static title
Without [] the effect reruns on every render needlessly

hints: useEffect takes a second argument after the callback.
Pass an empty array [] as that second argument to run the effect only on mount.
Write useEffect(() => { document.title = 'My Counter Program'; }, []); then click Add and watch the tab title stay the same.
common_mistakes: Leaving out the second argument, so the effect still runs on every render.
Putting [] inside the callback instead of passing it as useEffect's second argument.
Still using count in the title with [], then wondering why it never updates.
Forgetting to revert afterwards. The next step adds count as a dependency.

steps.title: Depend on count, add subtract
steps.instructions: In src/MyComponent.jsx use [count] as the useEffect dependency array so it runs on mount and when count changes. Add a Subtract button calling subtractCount, which does setCount(c => c - 1).

targets.caption: Dependency array now lists count
New handler that decrements count
Button wired to subtractCount

explanations.topic: Putting a value in the dependency array: run on mount plus when it changes
No dependency array vs [count]: avoid running on unrelated re-renders
Any change to count, up or down, re-runs the effect

hints: Look at the second argument to useEffect: put your state variable inside the empty array.
Write `}, [count]);` so the effect runs on mount and whenever count changes.
Copy addCount, rename it subtractCount, and use setCount(c => c - 1).
Add `<button onClick={subtractCount}>Subtract</button>` next to the Add button.
common_mistakes: Writing onClick={subtractCount()} which calls the function during render.
Leaving the dependency array empty [] so the title never updates after mount.
Passing count without array brackets, e.g. useEffect(fn, count).
Copying addCount but forgetting to change + 1 to - 1 or to rename the function.

steps.title: Add color state dependency
steps.instructions: Add a color state ('green') with a Change Color button toggling green/red, and style the count paragraph with style={{color: color}}. Include color in the title and use [count, color] as dependencies.

targets.caption: New color state variable, initially green
Handler flipping color via the previous state
Effect reruns when count or color changes
Button that toggles the count's color

explanations.topic: Updater function with previous state and a ternary to toggle values
Inline style needs double curly braces: JSX expression plus JS object
Without color in the dependency array, the title ignores color changes
Dependency array: effect runs whenever any listed value changes

hints: Create a second useState for color starting at 'green', and a button whose onClick calls a changeColor function.
In changeColor, call setColor with an updater: c => c === 'green' ? 'red' : 'green'.
Style the count paragraph with style={{color: color}}: the outer braces embed JS, the inner braces are the object.
Add color to the title template and change the dependency array to [count, color] so the title updates on color clicks too.
common_mistakes: Using single braces style={color: color}, which is a syntax error. The style prop needs an object inside the JSX braces.
Leaving the dependency array as [count], so the title doesn't change when the color toggles.
Writing onClick={changeColor()}, which calls it on render and causes an infinite re-render loop.
Using = instead of === in the ternary comparison, or misspelling 'green' so the toggle never flips back.
Forgetting to put color in the document.title template literal, so nothing visible changes in the tab title.

steps.title: Track window width and height
steps.instructions: Rewrite the component with width/height state from window.innerWidth/innerHeight, show them in px, and add window.addEventListener('resize', handleResize) plus a console.log directly in the component body. Run npm run dev and watch the console log repeat.

targets.caption: Resize handler updating width and height state
Rendered window dimensions in pixels

explanations.topic: State initialized from window.innerWidth / innerHeight
Display alone doesn't update on resize — need an event listener
Adding a listener in the component body runs on every render
Every re-render adds another listener — over 1,000 listeners

hints:
Create two state variables with useState, initialized to window.innerWidth and window.innerHeight, and render each in a

with 'px' after it.
Write function handleResize() with no parameters that calls setWidth(window.innerWidth) and setHeight(window.innerHeight).
In the component body (not inside useEffect), call window.addEventListener('resize', handleResize) and console.log('Event listener added').
Resize the browser window and open DevTools > Console: the log count should grow with every resize, which is the problem the next step fixes.
common_mistakes: Writing sethHeight / setheight with the wrong casing — the setter must be setHeight exactly as declared.
Calling handleResize() when passing it: addEventListener('resize', handleResize()) runs it immediately instead of passing the callback.
Using window.innerWidth for both state variables, so height shows the width value.
Forgetting to render the new component in App.jsx, so nothing appears on the page.
Expecting a single log line — in this step the listener is intentionally added on every render.

steps.title: Move listener into useEffect
steps.instructions: Wrap the addEventListener call and its console.log in useEffect with an empty dependency array [] so the listener is added only on mount. Check the console shows one addition (two in StrictMode).

targets.caption: Wrap the listener code in useEffect
Empty array = run only on mount

explanations.topic: Placing side-effect code inside useEffect
Empty dependency array runs the effect only on mount
StrictMode runs effects twice in development (setup + cleanup)

hints: Event listeners should be added once, not on every render. Which hook runs code after mount?
Move the addEventListener line and its console.log into the function you pass to useEffect.
Pass an empty array [] as the second argument to useEffect so it runs only on mount.
useEffect(() => { window.addEventListener("resize", handleResize); console.log("EVENT LISTENER ADDED"); }, []);
common_mistakes: Leaving out the dependency array, so the effect still runs after every render and keeps adding listeners
Calling handleResize() inside addEventListener instead of passing the function reference handleResize
Leaving a copy of addEventListener in the component body outside useEffect
Expecting exactly one log in StrictMode; two logs in development is normal
Forgetting to import useEffect from 'react'

steps.title: Return cleanup to remove listener
steps.instructions: Return a cleanup function from the effect that calls window.removeEventListener('resize', handleResize) and logs that the listener was removed. Refresh and confirm the StrictMode add/remove/add sequence in the console.

targets.caption: Cleanup function returned from useEffect
Remove the same listener with the same handler
StrictMode runs add, remove, add on mount

explanations.topic: Returning a function from useEffect is the cleanup mechanism
Cleanup runs before the next re-render or when the component unmounts
Why to remove event listeners on unmount (avoid unexpected behavior)
StrictMode runs the effect, cleans up immediately, then runs it again in development

hints: Inside the useEffect that adds the resize listener, add a return statement that returns a function.
In that returned arrow function, call window.removeEventListener with the same event name and handler you passed to addEventListener.
Add console.log("Event listener removed") inside the cleanup, then refresh and open DevTools > Console.
Expected order in StrictMode: added, removed, added.
common_mistakes: Calling removeEventListener directly in the effect body instead of inside a returned function.
Passing a new inline arrow function to removeEventListener instead of the same handleResize reference, so nothing is removed.
Writing return handleResize() or return removeEventListener(...), which runs it immediately instead of returning a function.
Misspelling the event name (e.g. 'resized') so it doesn't match the added listener.
Thinking the add/remove/add sequence is a bug when it is StrictMode's development double-invoke.

steps.title: Add second useEffect for title
steps.instructions: Add another useEffect that sets document.title = `Size: ${width} x ${height}` with dependency array [width, height]. Resize the window and confirm the title updates.

targets.caption: Second useEffect sets the tab title to the window size
Runs only when width or height changes

explanations.topic: A component can have more than one useEffect hook
Dependency array [width, height]: run on mount and when either changes
On mount the title shows the size right away, then updates on resize

hints: You can call useEffect more than once in the same component. Add a new one below the resize-listener effect.
Inside the callback, assign to document.title using a template string with ${width} and ${height}.
Pass a second argument, an array that lists both state variables, so the effect reruns only when they change.
Full form: useEffect(() => { document.title = `Size: ${width} x ${height}`; }, [width, height]);
common_mistakes: Using quotes instead of backticks, so the title literally reads ${width}.
Omitting the dependency array, so the title updates on every render.
Using an empty array [], so the title is set only once on mount.
Putting the title line inside the event-listener effect instead of adding a separate useEffect.
Writing document.Title (wrong case) so nothing changes.
